temporal_state_chain.observed: Ethan notices Gary working excessively long hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. When Ethan invites Gary to a weekend retreat, Gary declines, saying there is too much to do at the hospital.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is a dedicated, hardworking friend and doctor, but he has growing concern that Gary's work habits are harming his health.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. Gary's refusal reinforces that he is heavily committed to hospital work and may be unable or unwilling to step away, even when concerned friends intervene.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary is overcommitted to hospital work and at risk of neglecting his health; Gary may need continued support or another way to take a break.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To intervene supportively and help Gary prioritize his health, perhaps by finding another way to persuade or assist him.

temporal_state_chain.observed: During the retreat, Ethan observes Gary behaving restlessly and avoiding discussions about work.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary's overwork is mostly explained by hospital demands, though he remains concerned and hoped the retreat might help Gary relax.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. Gary's restlessness and avoidance make Ethan suspect that Gary's overwork is not solely due to professional obligations.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes there is something deeper behind Gary's overworking, likely a personal or emotional burden Gary has not shared.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To confront Gary gently and find out what is really going on so he can help.

temporal_state_chain.observed: Gary opens up about the pressures of managing a new department and the personal challenges he is facing.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan suspects there is more to Gary's overwork than professional obligations, but he does not yet know the specifics.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. Gary's disclosure confirms and clarifies Ethan's suspicion by revealing the pressures of the new department and personal challenges.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary is overwhelmed by new department responsibilities and personal difficulties, and he understands why Gary has been overworking.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To help Gary find a better balance by prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities.

temporal_state_chain.observed: Over the following months, Ethan regularly checks in with Gary. Gary reports that things are better, that he is not as overwhelmed, and that he even had time for a movie last weekend.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary needs ongoing support to build a healthier work-life balance, and that his help is still relevant.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. Gary's reports and visible efforts show that he is making real progress and becoming less overwhelmed.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary is improving and moving toward a healthier balance, though some challenges may remain.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To continue checking in, offering support, and encouraging Gary's progress.

temporal_state_chain.observed: After a year, Gary has successfully adjusted to a healthier work-life balance. Gary thanks Ethan, says he feels more in control, and appears capable of managing on his own.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary has been improving but may still need support or face occasional challenges.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. Gary's successful adjustment and sense of control show that he can now manage his life and work independently.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary is self-sufficient, doing well, and no longer needs active intervention, though Ethan remains willing to help if needed.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To step back and let Gary manage independently while remaining available if Gary ever needs him.
